# DocumentedForeachOverNonIterable

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report a `foreach` over a value that PHPDoc says is neither an array nor an
object. The loop may still run, since PHP does not check PHPDoc, but the loop
and the documentation disagree. Subjects the code alone proves are not
iterable are ForeachOverNonIterable's.

## Example

```php{5}
<?php
/** @param string $names */
function greet($names): void
{
    foreach ($names as $name) {
    }
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 5: Iterate over an array or an object, not string.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- The subject of a `foreach`.
- The type of the subject is the one PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var`, `@return` and `@property` tags count.
- Every member of that type is an int, a float, a string, a bool or null.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Subjects ForeachOverNonIterable reports.
- A subject of unknown type, or one that may be an array, an object,
  `iterable`, `callable` or `mixed`.
- A subject whose PHPDoc type the code contradicts: when the code
  alone gives the subject a type that no value of the PHPDoc type fits
  (`/** @var int $x */` over `$x = new Order()`), the tag is stale.
- `$this` inside a closure or an arrow function, which may be bound
  to an object of another class.

## Fix

None: either the loop or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

No gating.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedForeachOverNonIterable": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedForeachOverNonIterable
```
